quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.

options.text: Louder than
Quieter than
About as loud as

questions.correctAnswerText: Quieter than
questions.explanation: A motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it to keep you safe.

questions.question: Is it good to use all three lane positions?

options.text: No, because you will not get used to any part of a lane.
No, because it confuses other drivers.
Yes, if you are adapting to changing road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if you are adapting to changing road conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: If you carry a load on your motorcycle, where should it go?

options.text: Over the rear axle.
On the gas tank in front of you.
Against the sissy bar on the back of the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over the rear axle.
questions.explanation: Place loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You can go faster than the speed limit until the pass is done.
You can ignore no passing zone markings if you started in a passing zone.
You must follow the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must stay within the speed limit and only happen where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Follow closer to the vehicle ahead.
Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, increase your distance from other vehicles. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: How should you secure a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
On a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low to protect your motorcycle's balance.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you the light will turn red soon. Slow down and stop if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, should you move to the far part of your lane?

options.text: Yes, because you will be farther from them.
No, because it tells them to move back too soon.
It does not matter for safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because it tells them to move back too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far part of your lane when being passed. This may signal the passing driver to move back into your lane too early.

questions.question: What should you tell a passenger before they ride with you?

options.text: Get on before you start the engine.
Sit as far back as possible.
Stay quiet and avoid moving around.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay quiet and avoid moving around.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should board after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is put on the back of slow-moving vehicles. These vehicles go slower than 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: Tell your passenger to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.
Sit as far back on the motorcycle as possible.
Hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Keep their legs away from the muffler.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far back on the motorcycle as possible.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should get on only after the engine has started. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you. They should hold onto the passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chain, and other moving parts.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that increases their visibility.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce their reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, pick a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers. Cover the clutch and both brakes to reduce your reaction time. Slow down when approaching an intersection. Do not change your speed or position in a way that could confuse other drivers.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle responds to directional changes:

options.text: More slowly than usual.
More quickly than usual.
Normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to the motorcycle. The extra weight means the motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn than it normally would.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
Be able to keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. Shifting gears during a turn can cause a sudden change in power to the rear wheel and cause a skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly to help prevent skidding.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride more slowly than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: Ride carefully when approaching an intersection. Cover the clutch and both brakes to reduce your reaction time if you need to stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a factor in determining a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: A person's blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on body weight, the amount of alcohol consumed, and how quickly the alcohol is consumed. It is always safest to not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. They also make objects look farther away than they really are. Take time to get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has convex mirrors.

questions.question: The greatest potential for conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic is:

options.text: On the highway.
At intersections.
On rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk for conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles. Motorcyclists should be careful when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should maintain a following distance of at least:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second distance behind the vehicle in front of you under normal conditions. When conditions are not perfect, use a larger following distance.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: During broad daylight
At dusk
At night

questions.correctAnswerText: During broad daylight
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright colors and reflective gear when riding, even in daylight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: What should you do with the brakes when making a U-turn?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time
Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over
Use the front brake to keep the motorcycle stable

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can tip the bike over. Instead, use the rear brake to slow down while turning.

questions.question: What blood alcohol content (BAC) level makes a person legally intoxicated?

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person is legally intoxicated at 0.08 percent BAC or higher. You cannot legally drive a motor vehicle if you are intoxicated.

questions.question: You are passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic. Where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane
In the right portion of your lane
In the center of your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars on your right and there is no oncoming traffic. This keeps you away from opening car doors and people stepping out between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane for more space around you.
